basic_info.name: Apple Health (iOS Health app + HealthKit + Health Records) and Google Health Connect (+ Google Health app) — analyzed as one item: the OS-level health platforms
basic_info.category: Platform (OS-embedded health data layer + first-party health apps; not a lab nor a standalone interpreter)
basic_info.country: USA-headquartered, global distribution. Apple Health Records clinical-data ingestion is US-centric (plus UK/Canada since 2020); Health Connect is global Android; neither is tuned for Brazil (no BR lab/EHR native feeds, no Portuguese clinical content depth)
basic_info.stage: Public and mature as platform layers; AI-interpretation layer (Apple Project Mulberry / Google Health Coach) in flux — Apple's coach scaled back and delayed (Feb–May 2026), Google's coach live but fitness-centric and mid-backlash (May–Aug 2026)
basic_info.pricing_model: Apple: core Health app + Health Records + HealthKit free with iOS; Apple Fitness+ $9.99/month (changes under consideration per Bloomberg); planned 'Health+' subscription PIVOTED to free features inside the Health app per Eddy Cue decision (Apr 2026 reporting). Google: Health Connect free OS component (Android 9+/SDK 28+); Google Health app free; Fitbit Premium subscription continues [uncertain: current Fitbit/Google paid tier pricing and bundling under Google Health]; Samsung Health telehealth/premium workouts via partners (2025). No per-test pricing anywhere — platforms monetize hardware/subscription, not lab interpretation (yet)
basic_info.target_user: Mass consumer (every iPhone / Android user); Apple leans iPhone+Apple Watch owner in US/UK/CA for clinical records; Google leans Pixel/Fitbit/Android ecosystem. Neither targets clinicians as primary users
basic_info.scale_metrics: Apple: Health app preinstalled on all iPhones (active install base commonly cited >1.4B devices [uncertain: 2026 figure]); Health Records live since 2018 (US, VA 2019, UK/Canada 2020) with hundreds-to-1000+ institutions historically claimed [uncertain: current institutional count]; Apple Watch is the dominant health wearable. Google: Health Connect ships inside Android 14+ and is installable Android 9+ (billions of addressable devices [uncertain: exact count]); Google Health app forcibly replaced the Fitbit app ~May 2026 (Fitbit had ~tens of millions of active users [uncertain]) triggering review-bombing. Durable-threat read: distribution is unmatched, but as of Aug 2026 both platforms' LAB interpretation is delayed (Apple) or fitness-scoped (Google) — the platform threat is real but not yet landed; third-party AI (ChatGPT Health Jan 2026, Perplexity Health Mar 2026) is already riding these platforms as connectors, which is the faster-moving threat vector

product.core_features: Apple (iOS 26.x, Aug 2026): Health Records (FHIR download from connected health systems: labs, meds, immunizations, procedures, vitals), detailed lab results with reference ranges (since iOS 15, 2021) + Trends, medication tracking, Cycle Tracking, sleep/fitness dashboards, walking steadiness, AFib history, hypertension notifications (announced WWDC 2025, refining in watchOS 27), Workout Buddy AI coach (watchOS 27: works without iPhone, Spanish), iOS 26.4 (Mar 2026) added Bedtime Highlight and Blood Oxygen back to Vitals (post-Masimo). WWDC 2026 (iOS 27, fall 2026) shipped modest health set: perimenopause/menopause logging+education, faster data updates, synced step count, timezone-aware sleep — NO AI coach, NO redesign announced. Google: Health Connect = OS-level store/permission layer for fitness data (Jetpack 1.1.0 stable) + experimental Medical Records (FHIR); Google Health app (replaced Fitbit app May 2026) = redesigned dashboard + Google Health Coach AI ('Ask Coach') + nutrition/exercise/sleep + Fitbit device support; v5.05 (Aug 3, 2026) added Apple Health sync on iOS; Fitbit Labs AI experiments (May 2025): medical record navigator, symptom checker, unusual trends
product.signature_differentiator: Both own the DEFAULT OS health data layer: Apple HealthKit/Health Records and Health Connect are where every wearable, app and (increasingly) EHR record lands on the phone with user-granted permissions — no third party can match that position. Apple's unique piece: direct FHIR Health Records pipeline from hundreds of US/UK/CA health systems into the phone since 2018. Google's unique piece: Health Connect Medical Records — an OS-level, permissioned, FHIR R4/R4B store for medical records (labs as FHIR Observations with LOINC mapping, per-category read permissions, first-party browsing UI) — experimental but architecturally ahead of Apple in openness (any app can write/read with permission). The strategic signature: they don't need to win interpretation themselves — they can let ChatGPT Health / Perplexity Health connectors do it on top of their rails (Perplexity Health launched Mar 19, 2026 with an Apple Health connector + EHRs from a claimed 1.7M care providers)
product.lab_data_handling: Apple: labs arrive via Health Records (FHIR, US/UK/CA health systems) — displayed with reference ranges, flags and plain-language descriptions since iOS 15; Trends since iOS 15/16. NO AI interpretation of labs shipped as of Aug 2026 (Project Mulberry lab-explanation/coaching vision delayed); instead third-party AI connectors (Perplexity Health, ChatGPT Health) analyze Apple Health labs. No lab ordering, no retest cadence, no upload-your-own-PDF flow of record. Google: labs enter via Health Connect Medical Records API (FHIR R4/R4B; lab results = Observation with 'laboratory' FHIR category; LOINC-mapped; DiagnosticReport NOT supported; Observations outside known categories are dropped) — apps write medical data, user grants per-category read permission (READ_MEDICAL_DATA_LABORATORY_RESULTS), Health Connect provides browsing UI. Status Aug 2026: @ExperimentalPersonalHealthRecordApi, Jetpack 1.1.0-beta02, compile against Android 16 SDK — still experimental, Play policy still being drafted. Google Health app: medical-records UI present (via Fitbit lineage), Smart Health Links record sharing on roadmap; interpretation remains fitness/wellness coach, not labs. Cadence/hardware: both are passive receivers (EHR + wearables); no blood-test cadence model, no at-home testing economics
product.family_dependents_depth: Apple: essentially single-user per device; Apple Watch 'Family Setup' exists for kids/seniors but there is no dependent health-record aggregation, no pediatric reference-range handling, no hereditary-risk layer in the Health app. Google: Google Health has family features (friends/family sharing, child-account migration fixes on the 2026 roadmap incl. child-account deletion Jun 2026) — sharing mechanics, not clinical dependent management; no caregiver mode with clinical depth. Neither platform models family lab history or hereditary risk — a durable gap and a Dr. Exame pillar (family/dependent labs, caregiver view) that the platforms are structurally unlikely to own (their identity model is one Google/Apple ID = one person)
product.doctor_sharing: Apple: export/share health data as PDF from Health app; third-party apps and now AI connectors consume HealthKit with permission; no doctor-facing brief, no SOAP/consult-prep concept; physicians appear only as 'Practitioner' FHIR metadata inside records. Google: medical-record sharing via Smart Health Links is on the published roadmap (not yet live as of Jul 2026 roadmap); no clinician workflow. Both treat the doctor as an endpoint of a share, not a user — full white space for Dr. Exame's doctor portal/brief
product.action_loop_monetization: Apple: hardware (Apple Watch) + services (Fitness+ $9.99/mo; Health+ subscription plan pivoted — Cue decided to ship revamped Health features FREE inside the Health app, Apr 2026); Oakland content studio output to be repurposed 'as early as 2026'; no supplements, no telemedicine marketplace (wellness-video + coaching loop instead). Google: hardware (Pixel Watch, Fitbit incl. Fitbit Air) + subscription legacy (Fitbit Premium) + partnerships (Samsung Health added telehealth visits and premium workouts Sep 2025); Google Health Coach (AI) is the retention engine; roadmap adds CLI/'AI skills' on top of user health data and Smart Health Links. Neither sells lab tests nor supplements — their action loop is engagement+hardware lock-in, which means the post-interpretation commerce layer (tests, protocols, telemed) is still open

technology.ai_approach: Apple: on-device-first models; Workout Buddy (gen-AI fitness voice coach) shipped; Project Mulberry was to be an AI agent trained on data from Apple-hired physicians with educational content from sleep/nutrition/PT/mental-health/cardiology experts — scaled back Feb 2026 (leadership shakeup: Williams retired, Giannandrea retiring; health moved under Eddy Cue, ML folded under Federighi) and delayed to later iOS 27 cycle (possibly 27.1 Oct 2026 or 27.4 spring 2027); remaining near-term: AI chatbot using 'World Knowledge Answers' for wellness questions, revamped Siri supporting 'more advanced health-related queries' in iOS 27, camera-based walking/gait analysis, nutrition-label scanning via visual intelligence. Google: Gemini-era Google Health Coach ('Ask Coach') live in Google Health app (concise messages, charts in messages, log-by-chat being built); Fitbit Labs experiments (symptom checker, unusual trends, medical-record navigator); intent recognition before health answers. Both keep interpretation inside the wellness lane and avoid diagnosis claims — and both effectively outsource deep lab Q&A to third-party AI apps riding their APIs
technology.data_inputs: Apple: HealthKit (wearables, apps, manual), Health Records FHIR feeds from health systems (labs/meds/immunizations/procedures/vitals), nutrition logging coming (iOS 27 label scanning), iPhone camera (gait analysis upcoming). Google: Health Connect ecosystem (any third-party app: MyFitnessPal, Cronometer, LoseIt, Withings, Clue, Ultrahuman...), Fitbit/Pixel Watch devices, Medical Records API (FHIR) writers (e.g., records-portal apps), nutrition/sleep manual logging, 'Ask Coach' conversational logging. Neither ingests lab PDFs directly — records only arrive if an institution/app writes structured FHIR
technology.data_interoperability: The composite-moat question, Aug 2026 state: Apple — HealthKit read/write for all apps; Health Records on FHIR (Argonaut profiles) from connected institutions (US/UK/CA); Health Records API open to developers since 2018; third-party AI connectors now official pattern (Perplexity Health reads Apple Health; ChatGPT Health since Jan 2026); PDF export out. Google — Health Connect: fitness data types stable (Jetpack 1.1.0, Android 9+), Medical Records experimental FHIR R4/R4B store: 15 resource types (AllergyIntolerance, Condition, Observation(labs/vitals/pregnancy/social-history), Medication/Request/Statement, Patient, Practitioner/Role, Procedure, Immunization, Encounter/Location/Organization), fine-grained per-category permissions with a separate medical-records permission screen, first-party browsing UI, requires Android 16 SDK compile; Google Fit APIs sunset end-2026 (migration pressure into Health Connect); Smart Health Links sharing on Google Health roadmap; bidirectional Apple Health sync shipping (Google Health 5.05, Aug 2026). For Dr. Exame: these are EXHAUST surfaces to plug into (write normalized labs into Health Connect/HealthKit; read whatever users grant) and an INGESTION hedge — but in Brazil neither surface carries BR lab data (no native RNDS/lab connectors), so PDF extraction remains the only working BR ingestion path; watch Health Connect Medical Records GA as a future bridge from BR EHRs if/when local portals write FHIR
technology.platform: Apple: iOS/watchOS system apps + HealthKit/Health Records APIs (US/UK/CA institutional coverage). Google: Android OS component (Health Connect, Settings-integrated) + Google Health app on Android and iOS (5.05+) + Jetpack SDK for developers; Samsung Health parallel first-party app on Android also building records/telehealth

ux.onboarding: Apple: zero-friction (preinstalled); clinical records onboarding = find your health system in a directory and sign in with portal credentials — meaningful value only where institutions are connected (US/UK/CA). Google: Health Connect surfaces via Settings/OEM health apps; Google Health app forced-migration onboarding from Fitbit (May 2026) was the pain point — account-migration and data-loss confusion drove the backlash. Time-to-value is instant for wearable data, near-zero for labs unless your provider is connected — in Brazil effectively never
ux.data_visualization: Apple: Trends (multi-metric trend detection with highlights), Vitals panel (5 metrics incl. returned Blood Oxygen, iOS 26.4), Bedtime Highlight bar chart, reference-range flags on labs, interactive charts — the most polished consumer clinical-data visualization in market. Google: Google Health dashboard redesign (Today/Health tabs, customizable), sleep scores, exercise maps; Health Connect provides basic records browsing UI (functional, not analytical); AI Coach messages adding charts/maps per roadmap. Neither shows longitudinal lab trends with clinical framing (degree-of-abnormality, family context) — Apple Trends covers labs it has, but with no interpretation layer
ux.engagement_channel: Apple: OS-level — watch notifications, Workout Buddy voice coaching, Trends push, perimenopause notifications; engagement anchored in device, not in a service relationship; fitness streaks/rings. Google: Google Health Coach chat ('Ask Coach') is the retention bet — conversational daily logging and proactive messages (being tuned to be less chatty); Fitbit community/legacy streaks; push via Android. Neither has human-channel retention (no WhatsApp, no email relationship) — in BR terms, both are transactional platforms that third parties must animate

trust_gaps.clinical_validation_trust: Apple: positions as data display + wellness; FDA-cleared device features where it counts (ECG, AFib history; hypertension notifications framed as 'potentially life-saving'); perimenopause notifications explicitly 'not intended to replace traditional methods of diagnosis'; Mulberry training-by-physicians plan (Apple-hired doctors, expert content) shelved/delayed rather than shipped — no published accuracy methodology for any AI interpretation because none has launched. Google: Health Connect Medical Records is explicitly experimental (API annotation; Play policy still being written); Fitbit Labs AI features were opt-in experiments; Google Health Coach under active complaint-tuning (positivity vs objectivity). Risks: (1) scale + trust default — when they DO ship interpretation, 'good enough' wins; (2) third-party AI connectors on official rails (Perplexity/ChatGPT) get platform-blessed distribution without platform-level clinical governance; (3) data-loss/confusion during Google Health migration dented trust short-term. Credibility bar for Dr. Exame: publish methodology, keep non-diagnosis stance, show sources/citations per marker
trust_gaps.regulatory_posture: Apple: careful wellness-vs-device line — receives FDA clearances for specific watch features (ECG/AFib; hypertension path) while keeping the Health app informational; disclaimers on notifications; no diagnosis claims. Google: same posture — Health Connect is a data layer (device-agnostic), Coach is wellness; experimental labeling manages regulatory exposure; no FDA/ANVISA claims on records display. Neither is ANVISA RDC 657/2022-relevant in BR today (features not marketed as SaMD there); LGPD: both process health data under US/global terms — a Brazilian app with explicit LGPD posture + local hosting narrative differentiates. Dr. Exame's non-diagnosis compliance choice mirrors exactly the line both giants hold — validation that the ceiling is real and shared
trust_gaps.gaps_opportunities: What they do NOT do (Aug 2026) = Dr. Exame's window: (1) no AI lab interpretation shipped by either platform owner — Apple delayed (Mulberry scaled back Feb 2026, absent from WWDC 2026 keynote, maybe late iOS 27 cycle), Google Coach is fitness/wellness-scoped; (2) no lab-PDF ingestion — structured records only if an institution writes FHIR; Brazil's labs/portals don't, so platform rails are empty in BR while Dr. Exame's pdftotext pipeline works today; (3) no BR content: no Portuguese clinical explanations, no BR reference-range context; (4) no dependents/hereditary model (one account = one person); (5) no doctor brief/SOAP/consult-prep — doctor is a PDF recipient at best; (6) no retest cadence or action loop beyond fitness. What works (inspiration, not copy): Apple's Trends + plain-language lab descriptions (the UX bar for showing labs); Apple's per-category permission UX (consent granularity); Google's published roadmap practice (public expectation management after backlash); Google Health Connect's FHIR medical-records architecture (the shape of future ingestion — build the Dr. Exame side as a Health Connect Medical Records writer/reader NOW so GA-day the app is ready); Perplexity/ChatGPT connector pattern proves users want conversational interpretation over their records — Dr. Exame's chat already does this with local context. Strategic threat clock: Apple full interpretation ~2027 (iOS 27.4+) — 6-12 months of clear BR runway after that for localization depth; Google Gemini health push can move faster but is distracted by migration fallout
trust_gaps.relevance: Alta (High). Why: these two own the substrate every health app will sit on — HealthKit/Health Records and Health Connect Medical Records (FHIR) are becoming the canonical ingestion/exhaust surfaces, and the interpretation layer is visibly consolidating onto them (ChatGPT Health and Perplexity Health connectors already live on Apple Health, Mar 2026). Even though owner-operated lab interpretation is delayed (Apple) or shallow (Google) as of Aug 2026, Dr. Exame must (a) integrate as writer/reader on both rails, (b) win BR depth (PDF ingestion, Portuguese, LGPD, dependents, doctor brief) before either localizes, and (c) treat 'platform shows results with explanation' as the baseline UX being set globally
